verdict.rationale: Supabase Database Webhooks let users define table-event rules (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) that automatically send HTTP requests to any endpoint, including Edge Functions. They are built on triggers and pg_net, so event-driven automation is directly documented. Coverage is limited to database table events, and Cron is a time-based schedule rather than an event trigger, so it does not count toward this story. missing for 10: documented event triggers beyond table row changes (e.g., auth or storage events), conditional rule logic or filtering in the webhook definition, an AI-native or agent-facing way to define these rules, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Database Webhooks allow you to send real-time data from your database to another system whenever a table event occurs.
You can hook into three table events: `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, and `DELETE`. All events are fired *after* a database row is changed
They can be used for listening to webhooks
